newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin to sell majority stake in Bewag.
newsitem.headline: Berlin to sell majority stake in Bewag.

text.p: Berlin said on Tuesday it would sell its majority stake in power utility Berliner Kraft und Licht AG (BEWAG) to a German-American consortium for 3.19 billion marks ($1.9 billion).

Annette Fugmann-Heesing, finance senator for the financially strapped city-state, said that Southern Co of the United States, plus Germany's Veba AG and Viag AG would be acquiring Berlin's stake in the monopoly for 2.9 billion marks.
The three companies will pay Berlin another 290 million marks for additional, unspecified factors.
Several Berlin senators had complained that BEWAG was worth much more than 2.9 billion marks and could not possibly be sold for less than three billion marks.
Berlin, which is struggling to plug a five billion mark deficit in its 45 billion mark budget this year, will attempt to sell nearly six billion marks of holdings in 1997.
Southern will receive a 23.6 percent stake and management control of the company, Fugmann-Heesing said.
Veba and Viag, which already hold 10 percent stakes, will each receive an additional 13.6 percent, making their total stakes equal to Southern's.
Fugmann-Heesing said the three companies pledged to hold the 50.8 percent of the company for a minimum of 20 years.
If the sale is completed by the end of the year, the three buyers will receive this year's dividend, she said. Berlin received a dividend payment of 45 million marks in 1996.

The sale will be submitted first to European Union cartel authorities where Fugmann-Heesing said she expected a favourable ruling. If the case were referred to German cartel authorities, however, she said she feared a negative judgment.
The German anti-trust agency has already expressed its doubts about the sale.

"The European cartel authorities will examine the sale first," Fugmann-Heesing said. "I expect a positive decision. But if there is a decision to pass the sale to the German cartel agency, then I expect it to be rejected."
Berlin had hoped that numerous German and foreign utilities would compete in an aggressive round of bidding for BEWAG.
But many potential foreign bidders dropped out of the running when it emerged that Veba and Viag had acquired rights of first refusal more than 50 years ago.
Rather than bid against each other, Veba, Viag and Southern Co made a joint bid for BEWAG.

Analysts estimated that Berlin's BEWAG stake was worth at least 3.3 billion marks and some said the company, which is nearing completion of an expensive modernisation of its infrastructure in east Berlin, could have fetched four billion marks or more.
BEWAG provides electricity and heating for more than two million households in Berlin's 3.4 million people, and for thousands of companies as well.

It had sales of 4.25 billion marks last year and a net profit of 170 million marks. Electricity in Berlin costs 22.68 pfennigs per kilowatt hour -- the highest price in Germany. ($ = 1.705 German Marks)
